<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

On proxied (BYOK) Copilot seats, Copilot 1.0.114's client-side generic tool search leaves deferred tools out of the tools array until they are activated, then drops them again. availableToolCount swung between 30 and 50, and tools lead the cached prefix, so every swing re-wrote the whole prompt at the 1-hour price (86% of hot same-process flips re-wrote more than half the prompt). The fix is a setting, not code. `toolSearch: false` cannot be set from a repo, so the prime applied it user-wide in ~/.copilot/settings.json on Jordan's go at 2026-11-19T03:27:46Z; this PR contains none of it. This plan measures the fix on a canary and on the fleet, measures its price (a larger tool prefix) and the flips it leaves (reload token-only flips, and a +5-tool first change in one resumed process), and re-prices egret's windows. The achievable estimate keeps those residual flips, and an optimistic bound removes every flip. It also weighs a per-seat cache TTL in the proxy: that doesn't pay, so every seat keeps 1h and nothing is built. The after-window is a loss: with the residual flips kept, the proxy re-prices at 11.2% more than plain after #243 (it saves 8.5% only in the cold-wake-heavy week before), while the first measured hour after the setting saves 11.8% against plain in steady state and costs 7.3% more with the restart re-writes included (n=474; sim232.md § Measured after the setting). Whether to keep the proxy is a decision for the prime and Jordan, outside plan 232.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Proxied seats keep a fixed tool list, so a hot turn reads its prompt from cache instead of re-writing it.
- The fleet's cost with the fix is known in egret's terms: against plain, against the proxy as it ran, and part by part.
- The per-seat TTL question is answered with numbers and closed.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- No proxy, daemon or CLI code. The fix is a Copilot setting the prime applied user-wide; this PR only documents and measures it.
- No fix for the extensions_reload token-only flip (a known residual, below).
- No change to the shared sidecar, its config or LaunchAgent, or the prod daemon.
- No per-request TTL mix: takin's spike showed a 1h marker read over a 5m entry never upgrades it.
- No decision on keeping or dropping the proxy: that belongs to the prime and Jordan.

<a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

Cause (pm-004, confirmed by the prime). On the BYOK Anthropic route, Copilot 1.0.114 runs client-side generic tool search (flag copilot_cli_tool_search_client_generic). Deferred tools stay out of the tools array until activated and are dropped again afterwards (copilot_cli_tool_deferral_sticky null). A bash call adds the 5 async-shell companions, and extensions_reload adds 1 or removes 5. On CAPI, hosted tool search keeps the array fixed. Setting scope: `copilot config --local toolSearch false` refuses, because toolSearch is not among the settings a repo may override, and neither a flag nor an env var sets it. Copilot reads settings.json only at process start, so seats started before 03:27:46Z keep their old tool search until restarted. Canary (assets/canary-sessions.md): proxied opus 23fd00ea held 49 tools on all 18 requests, and its hot writes were 96-423 tokens (0.2-0.9%). The first extensions_reload changed toolTokenCount from 30,846 to 36,528 and back with the count unchanged, costing one full re-write (48,911) and a 20.6% one. The second reload changed nothing. The prime's haiku canary e6499e1f held 49 over 5 requests. Fleet residuals under the setting (fresh processes, same process): e69a6a28 was resumed at 03:30:18Z. Its first request carried 44 tools (28,931 tool tokens) and the next one, after its first bash call, carried 49 (30,846; +1,915, the size of the async-shell set). That re-wrote 273,951 tokens (222 AIU billed). It happened in 1 of 11 resumed processes. 9da2c60e repeated the reload token-only flip right after its resume (190 AIU over 2 records). Price of the fix: tool definitions grow from 17,913 to 30,846 tokens on every request. Fresh seats now read about 34.4k of shared prefix (system and tools) that other seats wrote. Restart cost: the first request after a restart re-writes the whole prompt once (7c8a587b: 300,980 of 335,398). Sim (assets/sim232.md). Historical flips: 126, of which 50 are residual-class (15 token-only, 30 right after a reload, 5 first change in a resumed process). The achievable estimate removes 42 (6,066 of 6,327 AIU billed), and the bound removes 87 (12,060 of 12,584). Egret's method against plain: achievable +8.5% saving before #243 and -11.2% after, bound +26.3% and +7.3%, and the proxy as it ran -10.2% and -27.5%. Opus <5 min costs 35.1 AIU/1M achievable and 26.4 bound, against plain's 22.5. The 5-60 min cell is thin (n=94). The mechanistic segment-cache sim is within +5.3% of billed for the proxied sessions as they ran. Achievable is -11.5% against that, and the bound -27.3%. Per-seat TTL: against 1h for all, every buildable policy costs 5.9-24.2% more before #243 and 7.2-11.3% after, and a per-seat hindsight bound saves only 0.9% and 5.4%. Live after-window at 04:28Z (sim232.md, flip-window.md), proxied main-agent requests: Before the setting: same-process flip rate 3.40% (82 count + 9 token-only of 2,710). Processes started after it (17, 13 of them resumed): 1.09% (1 count, e69a6a28, + 4 token-only, two reloads, of 470); one of these processes holds a steady 36 tools without flipping. Old processes after the setting: 1.91% (4 count of 209). Measured cost against plain, same method: Fresh processes, steady state (each process's first request excluded): 3,539 AIU billed against 4,011 as plain, +11.8% (n=457). Opus hot cell -30.4% (n=319); opus 5-60 min cell +91.5% (n=16). Including the 17 restart re-writes: 5,716 against 5,329, -7.3%. Old processes: +27.9% (n=209). One hour of data: the steady state beats plain, while the achievable model says -11.2% for the after-#243 window. The difference is cold wakes, which the model prices from a thin cell.

## Execution Guardrails

- Worktree fleet-232-proxy-tool-flips, branch coder/232-proxy-tool-flips; edits by absolute path.
- Usage fields only: no session text, no credential files, no tokens in outputs. Scripts read $HOME, with no hard-coded user paths.
